free_tier.stated: 1 GB / month of data transfer out, 20,000 HTTP requests / month and 5,000 TCP connections / month, counted by the ngrok free plan that the operator's authtoken belongs to; up to 3 online endpoints
free_tier.notes: The operator itself meters nothing; the byte cap is the ngrok account plan of the authtoken in the Ngrok resource.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: counted per month rather than per object

egress.terms: metered at 1 GB / month on the free ngrok plan; the first paid plan, Hobbyist, includes 5 GB and adds more against credit; pay-as-you-go is 5 GB included, then $0.10/GB

interface_detail: a Kubernetes custom resource of kind Ngrok (apiVersion ngrok.com/v1alpha1) with protocol http or tcp, applied with kubectl; the operator is installed with Helm
tooling: the user installs and runs the operator, a Helm chart, in a Kubernetes cluster that they supply; the tunnels it creates are relayed by ngrok's hosted edge
chaining: the byte volume is relayed by the hosted ngrok service (see egress/ngrok-free for its free plan); the operator only creates and renews the tunnel from a cluster

limits.value: 1 GB per month of data transfer out; 20,000 HTTP requests, 5,000 TCP connections, 10,000 log events and 500 webhook verifications per month, on the ngrok free plan
4,000 HTTP requests per minute and 100 TCP connections per minute on the ngrok free plan, separate from the monthly quotas

limits_note: the allowance is a byte volume over a period, which none of the six kinds names; the number is in egress.free_allowance. Up to 3 online endpoints and 1 development domain on the free plan.
binding_note: 1 GB per month on the free ngrok plan is about 1,100 times below 1 TiB, so the byte quota fails first; the first paid plan, Hobbyist at $10 monthly, includes 5 GB.

identity_cost.detail: an ngrok account and its authtoken, which the Ngrok resource takes in spec.authtoken; TCP endpoints on the free plan need a valid payment method added to the account; the sign-up form fields are unverified: behind a sign-up

reliability_note: the last commit of the repository is dated 10 March 2023 (a dependency bump) and its example resources point at ngrok.io hostnames; no commit for more than three years
confidence_note: Operator behaviour is read from its README and example resource; the byte cap is read from the first-party ngrok plan pages. No tunnel was run, because that needs an ngrok account.

evidence.quote: Ngrok operator provide developer easy access to private Kubernetes cluster for testing purpose via ngrok.
evidence.proved: the project is a Kubernetes operator that creates ngrok tunnels, not a relay of its own

evidence.quote: # protocol used, currently support http & tcp
evidence.proved: the operator supports the http and tcp protocols only
every Ngrok resource carries an ngrok account authtoken
the ngrok free plan caps data transfer out at 1 GB per month

evidence.proved: Free is 1 GB, Hobbyist includes 5 GB, pay-as-you-go is 5 GB then $0.10/GB

evidence.proved: TCP tunnels on the free plan need a payment method on the account

extras.transit_note: the operator runs the ngrok agent in a pod and ngrok's edge relays the bytes, which is what the 1 GB monthly counter counts

notes: MIT licensed. The ngrok project's own Kubernetes operator is a different product that the free plan page lists as included on all plans. This record is the community operator by zufardhiyaulhaq; its tunnel capacity is the ngrok plan of the authtoken.
